symptom: ako/mxcli#2100 (mendixlabs/mxcli#1805): a .test.mdl test calling a microflow with Apply entity access = Yes failed CE0114 at build ('A microflow that does not apply entity access can only call microflows that also do not apply entity access') and MDL-SEC22 at check; the same for an applying @setup. Making the generated test microflow apply entity access then failed CE0150 on the runner's own handlers ('attributes of System.Error … cannot be accessed in microflows that apply entity access').
cause: Three generators wrote callers without the setting: writeTestFlow (endpoint), GenerateTestRunner (legacy MxTest.TestRunner) and CheckSource (MxTest.Check_* wrappers). The runner's verdict and @throws handlers read $latestError/Message directly, which an applying flow may not.
file: cmd/mxcli/testrunner/caller_entity_access.go (callerAppliesEntityAccess, errorMessageFlow helper), generator_endpoint.go (attachOnError numbers its handlers), generator.go, check_source.go, runner.go (legacy cleanup), build_attribution.go
insight: CE0114 has one direction, so the safe constant is 'apply' (the same call RegisterEndpoint made for #1654) — but the setting has a second, opposite constraint (CE0150), and the fix has to be measured against both: mx check on 11.12.1 at Off and Production showed an applying flow reading an ordinary entity's attribute is 0 errors, so CE0150 is the only cost. Mendix's CE0150 text prescribes the helper. The runtime half needs no measurement because the endpoint runs tests under Core.createSystemContext. A test body that reads $latestError/ itself is the one case 'apply' would newly break, so it keeps the old setting; under the legacy runner that decision is per suite because all tests share one microflow. The reported fix named two generators; the legacy runner was a third.
